pages.name: Home
pages.content: Hilltop News collects links worth reading and the discussion around them. The latest stories are on the news page.

pages.name: Guidelines
pages.content:
Be kind. Link to the original source. Say what you learned, not what you feel.

Comments that only insult are removed.

pages.name: FAQ
pages.content:
Questions and answers about how the site works.

Is there an account? Not to read. To comment you give a name and an email address; the address is never shown.

hn-story.name: Ask: how do you keep a small team's on-call sane?
hn-story.excerpt: Ask: how do you keep a small team's on-call sane?

comments.author: mkersten
comments.body:
Two rules saved us: nobody carries the pager two weeks in a row, and every page that was not actionable gets deleted the next morning.

The second one cut our pages by half in a month.

replies.author: quietops
replies.body: How do you decide what counts as actionable? We argue about that more than we fix things.

replies.author: lindqvist
replies.body: If the runbook step is wait and see, it is not a page. It is a ticket.

replies.author: saoirse
replies.body: That rule is easy to say and hard to enforce when a customer is on the phone.

replies.author: tomasz
replies.body: We moved the phone to a separate rota. Engineers only get paged when the alert has a named owner and a first step.

replies.author: quietops
replies.body: That is a good split. Writing the first step down was the hard part for us.

comments.author: pg_reader
comments.body:
A short script that lists last week's pages sorted by how often they fired helped us pick what to delete:

psql -At -c "select alert, count(*) from pages where fired_at > now() - interval '7 days' group by alert order by 2 desc limit 20" example_ops_database_with_a_long_connection_string

attributes.text: We are five engineers and a pager. Rotations burn people out within a quarter. What has actually worked for you, and what did you stop doing?

hn-story.name: Eight siblings: what does your release checklist look like?
hn-story.excerpt: Eight siblings: what does your release checklist look like?

comments.author: saoirse
comments.body: I would start with the simplest thing: a shared calendar and a rule that swaps are always honoured.

comments.author: mkersten
comments.body: Our pager rotation is one week in six. Anything more frequent and people stopped answering.

comments.author: tomasz
comments.body: Write a runbook for every alert, or delete the alert. There is no third option.

comments.author: lindqvist
comments.body: Pay for it. Time off in lieu works better than a bonus.

comments.author: pg_reader
comments.body: We keep a log of every night wake-up and review it monthly. Numbers end arguments.

replies.author: quietops
replies.body: Do you share the numbers with the whole team?

comments.author: quietops
comments.body: Follow-the-sun is the real fix, if you can hire for it. A team of five cannot.

comments.author: saoirse
comments.body: Test the pager. A page that goes to a phone on silent is the same as no page.

comments.author: mkersten
comments.body: Shadow shifts for new people before they carry it alone made a big difference.
